entities.evidence: The directional ending and the verb “enter” identify Egypt as Abram’s destination, the land named in Genesis 12:10.
Abram addresses Sarai as his wife. Genesis 11:29 names her as Abram’s wife, and Genesis 17:15 identifies Sarah as her later name.

review.translation: [And it happened|0] [that as|1] [he was about|2] [to enter|3] [Egypt|4], [he said|5] [to|6] [Sarai|7], [his wife|8], “[Look|9] [now|10], [I know|11] [that|12] [you|16] {are} [a woman|13] [beautiful|14] [in appearance|15].

analysis.evidence: וַיְהִי introduces the episode impersonally. The כַּאֲשֶׁר clause sets the time, as Abram drew near to Egypt, and וַיֹּאמֶר gives the main event, his speech to Sarai.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ introduces יְהִי, the short third-person masculine singular Qal form of הָיָה, in a wayyiqtol construction.

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 68612:2, 67605:30, 67344:6, 67337:9.
analysis.morphology: Relative particle with prefixed comparative preposition כַּ.
analysis.sense: with a preposition: as, where, than, until

analysis.evidence: In כַּאֲשֶׁר הִקְרִיב לָבוֹא מִצְרָיְמָה, Abram himself draws near. The infinitive phrase לָבוֹא מִצְרָיְמָה specifies what he is close to doing, entering Egypt.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil perfect, third person masculine singular, with Abram as the subject.

analysis.evidence: In הִקְרִיב לָבוֹא מִצְרָיְמָה, the infinitive specifies what Abram was about to do. The directional ending on מִצְרָיְמָה identifies Egypt as the land he was about to enter.
analysis.morphology: The preposition לָ־ prefixes the Qal infinitive construct of בּוֹא.

analysis.evidence: הִקְרִיב לָבוֹא describes Abram drawing near to enter Egypt. מִצְרָיְמָה names the land he was approaching.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with directional ה. The ending ־ָה marks Egypt as the destination.
Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־

draft.change: Add Genesis 15:7 as an example of the existing sense to-a-person-speaking for אֶל.
draft.definition: With a verb of speaking, אֶל marks the person addressed.
draft.evidence: In Genesis 15:7, וַיֹּאמֶר אֵלָיו introduces Yahweh’s words to Abram. The third-person suffix names the addressee from the narrator’s perspective, and Yahweh addresses him in the second person in הוֹצֵאתִיךָ.

analysis.evidence: In וַיֹּאמֶר אֶל שָׂרַי אִשְׁתּוֹ, “he said to Sarai his wife,” אֶל introduces Sarai as Abram’s addressee.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew preposition without a prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for שָׂרַי linked to the שׂרר word family.
draft.definition: Sarai, the earlier name of Abram’s wife Sarah.
draft.evidence: Genesis 11:29 names Abram’s wife Sarai. Genesis 17:15 gives both names when God tells Abraham to call her Sarah.

analysis.evidence: In וַיֹּאמֶר אֶל שָׂרַי אִשְׁתּוֹ (‘he said to Sarai his wife’), אֶל introduces the person Abram addresses, and אִשְׁתּוֹ identifies her as his wife.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: The personal name of Abram’s wife before she was named Sarah.

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 68613:4, 66585:4, 66577:3, 66561:4, 66324:3.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular construct noun with the third-person masculine singular possessive suffix ־וֹ.

analysis.evidence: Abram uses הִנֵּה נָא to draw Sarai’s attention to the statement יָדַעְתִּי כִּי אִשָּׁה יְפַת מַרְאֶה אָתְּ, “I know that you are a beautiful woman.” He presents her beauty as a fact he already knows.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew demonstrative particle used as an interjection. It has no prefix or suffix. The following נָא is a separate particle.
analysis.sense: see now (a fact put before the hearer)

analysis.evidence: נָא follows הִנֵּה. Together they mean “see now” and draw Sarai’s attention to Abram’s statement יָדַעְתִּי כִּי, “I know that…”
analysis.morphology: Hebrew particle of entreaty with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The כִּי clause gives the content of Abram’s knowledge. He tells Sarai, “I know that you are a beautiful woman.”
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, first person common singular. The ending ־תִּי marks Abram as the speaker. The perfect expresses his present state of knowledge.
analysis.sense: to know that something is the case

analysis.evidence: After יָדַעְתִּי (“I know”), כִּי introduces the clause אִשָּׁה יְפַת־מַרְאֶה אָתְּ (“you are a beautiful woman”), which states what Abram knows about Sarai.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected Hebrew conjunction with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: that (what is seen, known or said)

analysis.evidence: Abram says to Sarai, אִשָּׁה יְפַת מַרְאֶה אָתְּ, “you are a beautiful woman.” The earlier אִשְׁתּוֹ identifies her as his wife. Here יְפַת מַרְאֶה describes her appearance.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular common noun in the absolute state, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: Abram tells Sarai, אִשָּׁה יְפַת מַרְאֶה אָתְּ, “you are a woman beautiful in appearance.” The noun מַרְאֶה specifies the respect in which she is beautiful.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular adjective agreeing with אִשָּׁה, in the construct state before מַרְאֶה.

analysis.evidence: Abram calls Sarai אִשָּׁה יְפַת מַרְאֶה, “a woman beautiful in appearance.” The noun specifies the respect in which she is beautiful.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute noun completing the construct phrase יְפַת מַרְאֶה.

analysis.evidence: Abram addresses Sarai, his wife. In אִשָּׁה יְפַת מַרְאֶה אָתְּ, the final pronoun is the subject of the clause, and the preceding phrase describes her: “you are a woman of beautiful appearance.”
analysis.morphology: Independent second-person feminine singular pronoun in its pausal form.
analysis.sense: you (are): the woman addressed named or identified
